candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9 / PDF p.13
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate an evidence-insufficient routine scoliosis screening recommendation from evaluation of symptomatic or visibly affected adolescents.

options.A: The USPSTF concludes that evidence is insufficient to determine the balance of benefits and harms of routine screening in this asymptomatic age group
options.B: The USPSTF recommends routine screening of every asymptomatic adolescent with a Grade A recommendation
options.C: The USPSTF recommends against all evaluation for scoliosis, including adolescents with obvious spinal deformity or symptoms
options.D: A school screening test by itself establishes the definitive diagnosis and Cobb angle

candidate.rationale: The current USPSTF recommendation is an I statement for asymptomatic children and adolescents aged 10 to 18 years: evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening. The page notes that literature scans through January 2025 did not identify new evidence warranting an updated review. This recommendation does not apply to symptomatic clients or those with obvious deformity.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Supports an I statement for routine screening of asymptomatic ages 10–18 and distinguishes screening from diagnostic radiography.
candidate.source_version_date: January 9, 2018; literature surveillance through January 2025; accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A school health team asks whether current USPSTF evidence supports routine screening of all asymptomatic adolescents ages 10 to 18 years for idiopathic scoliosis. Which response is most accurate?

warning: Technical candidate selection only. This file is not clinical audit evidence and does not establish PASS or FAIL.
